Both clean and onion architecture require dependencies to point inward, with inner layers unaware of outer ones.
Domain entities should be framework- and persistence-agnostic, relying only on PHP itself and the standard library.
Controllers and templates belong to the presentation/interface layer; business logic resides in the domain/application layer (use cases).
In onion architecture, the innermost layer is the domain model (entities/business logic), with dependencies pointing inward toward it.
Tools like deptrac analyze dependencies between layers and fail the build when forbidden calls are detected.
In clean architecture, use cases should receive plain data (DTOs/primitives) and abstractions via dependency injection, not framework-specific objects like HTTP requests or EntityManagers.
A Repository provides a collection-like interface over aggregates/entities while encapsulating the storage mechanism.
Databases are infrastructure concerns in the outer layer, isolated behind interfaces so the domain and use cases remain independent.
An aggregate is a cluster of domain objects treated as a single consistency boundary unit, not merely a database table.
Value Objects are defined by their attribute values, are immutable, and equality is based on field values rather than object identity.
In DDD, the aggregate root is the sole entry point through which all modifications to the aggregate must pass.
Repositories are defined per aggregate root, since only aggregates as a whole are loaded and persisted.
Ubiquitous language is a DDD term referring to a shared vocabulary used by both developers and domain experts.
A vocabulary defines the boundary of consistent meaning for a model and its language, while outside it the same words may refer to different models.
DDD recommends a rich domain model with behavior on the entities, not anemic models where logic lives only in services.
In domain-driven design, each bounded context maintains its own model, so the same real-world concept may be represented by different classes in different contexts.

Symfony's compiled DI container instantiates services only when they are first requested, unless a service is marked as public/synchronous eager initialization or configured otherwise (e.g., via S plage compiler or 'lazy' proxies for interface-based laziness).
The Symfony command `php bin/console debug:router` lists all registered routes.
Autowiring automatically injects services by type-hinting, so most services don't need manual declaration in services.yaml.
Twig compiles templates into plain PHP classes and caches them for reuse across requests.
In dev, Symfony checks tracked container-related files on each request but only recompiles the container when one of them changes.
Symfony reads the APP_ENV environment variable to determine the active environment (dev, prod, etc.).
Symfony controller methods must be public because the service container / routing needs to call them from outside the class.
Subscribers and listeners are dispatched in the same flow; priority comes from explicitly configured priority, not from implementing the subscriber interface.
Symfony 6.0 removed the Guard system in favor of authenticators based on AuthenticatorInterface.
The #[IsGranted] attribute (SensioFrameworkExtraBundle / Symfony security) denies access with a 403 when the role/voter requirement fails.
Symfony Voters are indeed the mechanism for authorization decisions on specific objects via isGranted().
Symfony 7 removed doctrine/annotations support for validation, so constraints must be declared using PHP attributes.
Symfony forms enable CSRF protection by default and automatically validate the token on submission.
Symfony validation always runs server-side on form submission, regardless of client-side HTML5 validation results.
Symfony's maker bundle provides `make:form` to generate a form type class.
Symfony stores only the user's identifier and roles in the session, never the password.
Symfony stores bundle configuration as separate files in the config/packages directory, typically one per bundle or topic.
Symfony best practice is to commit .env with safe development defaults while keeping real secrets in the git-ignored .env.local.
The `php bin/console debug:container` command lists registered services and their aliases in the service container.
Once the container is compiled and running, it is frozen, so setParameter() throws an exception and cannot be used from a controller.
Since Symfony 3.4/4.0, services are private by default and can only be accessed via dependency injection, not fetched directly from the container.
Bundles work with sensible defaults; configuration in config/packages is only needed to override defaults.
In Symfony, %env(VAR)% in services.yaml is replaced with the value of the environment variable VAR.
Symfony uses the APP_DEBUG environment variable (typically set in .env) to enable debug mode, which activates the profiler and Twig debugging.
Symfony Messenger allows a message to be handled by multiple handlers via different buses or handler configuration.
The sync transport handles messages immediately in the same process, without queueing them for a worker.
Symfony's worker that processes Messenger queues is started with `php bin/console messenger:consume`.
In Symfony Messenger, the retry_strategy option is set on each transport in the framework.messenger.transports configuration, so retries are configured per transport.
Symfony Messenger's default serializer uses PHP's native serialize() format (PhpSerializer), not JSON.
Symfony's Scheduler component schedules messages and sends them through Messenger transports to be handled by handlers.
The doctrine/messenger transport (messenger.transport.doctrine / Doctrine DBAL bridge) stores queued messages in database tables via Doctrine.
Symfony Messenger allows adding custom middleware to the stack, positioned before or after built-in middleware.
Symfony releases a major version every two years and minor versions every six months, in May and November.
Symfony 8.0 requires PHP 8.4 or higher, following its policy of supporting the last two PHP major versions.
Symfony 7.0 dropped support for docblock annotations, requiring PHP attributes instead.
Symfony's AssetMapper serves CSS/JS modules directly using importmap.php, requiring no Node.js or webpack.
Symfony 6.4 is an LTS release with extended support (until 2027).
Symfony removes features deprecated in the previous major branch when a new major version is released.
Each Symfony major release ships with an UPGRADE guide describing all breaking changes.
Symfony's AssetMapper component manages assets and importmaps natively without Node.js or webpack.

Symfony releases a minor version every six months, so 8.2 (May 2026) is the version that follows 8.1.
Symfony releases follow backward-compatible versioning, and upgrades do not require complete rewrites of application APIs.

Twig templates are sandboxed and cannot call arbitrary PHP functions directly; only whitelisted functions and filters are available.
Twig enables HTML auto-escaping by default when rendering output, unless configured otherwise.
The |e filter escapes a string for safe output, defaulting to HTML context.
The format_number filter from twig/intl-extra formats a number according to a given locale using PHP's intl NumberFormatter.
In Twig, the |raw filter marks a value as safe, preventing it from being auto-escaped.
{{ }} outputs expression values, while {% %} executes Twig tags like if, for, and set.
Twig allows declaring variables inside templates using the {% set %} tag.
Twig's dump() function outputs the debug structure of a variable when debug mode is enabled.
Bootstrap provides CSS/JS UI components (grid, buttons, modals) and is not a single-page application framework like Angular or React.
The .container class is responsive with a fixed max-width at each breakpoint, unlike .container-fluid which spans full width.
The Bootstrap grid uses 12 columns, not 16, though it is historically based on CSS floats.
The smallest breakpoint (xs) uses no infix, so the named infixes are exactly sm, md, lg, xl, and xxl — five of them.
In Bootstrap, spacing utilities like .mt-3 multiply the base $spacer variable (1rem) by the given number.
Bootstrap 5 uses data-bs-toggle to initialize interactive components like dropdowns.
Bootstrap 5 removed the jQuery dependency and its components are written in vanilla JavaScript.
Bootstrap dark mode is enabled with the data-bs-theme="dark" attribute, not a .dark class.
Doctrine ORM requires the schema to be created explicitly (e.g., via migrations or the schema tool); it does not create tables automatically at runtime.
EntityManager::persist() schedules an entity for management, with SQL executed only at flush().

DQL (Doctrine Query Language) is object-oriented and operates on entities, their fields, and relationships rather than database tables and columns.
Doctrine's find() returns null when no matching record exists.

HTTP 204 No Content indicates a successful request with no response body.

HTTP 429 Too Many Requests indicates the client has sent too many requests in a given time (rate limiting).

Use hash_equals() or password_verify() to compare hashes, since == is not timing-safe.

The CSP header is set via the Content-Security-Policy HTTP header.

Refresh tokens have a longer lifetime and are used to request new access tokens without re-authenticating the user.
Salts are not secret; they're stored alongside the hash and are only needed to prevent precomputed rainbow table attacks.
PHPUnit only runs test methods in classes that extend TestCase.
setUp() runs before each test method; setUpBeforeClass() runs once before all tests.
A data provider supplies multiple sets of arguments, so the test runs once for each set.
